plan.intro: Day 1: Zion Canyon Visitor Center; Human History Museum. Day 2: Kolob Canyons Visitor Center; Human History Museum. Day 3: Zion-Mt. Carmel Highway; Human History Museum. Day 4: Zion Nature Center; Human History Museum.

days.label: Zion Canyon orientation and the museum views

stops.name: Zion Canyon Visitor Center
stops.note: Start near the South Entrance; use the outdoor exhibits and ask a ranger which canyon outings make sense for your dates.
stops.why: It gives you a useful first look before committing the rest of the trip to an outing whose access may vary.

stops.name: Human History Museum
stops.note: See the exhibits and 22-minute orientation film, then step outside for views of the Towers of the Virgin and Bridge Mountain.
stops.why: The museum pairs an introduction to Zion’s human history with a distinctly scenic stop on your first day.

days.label: Kolob Canyons and a slower canyon afternoon

stops.name: Kolob Canyons Visitor Center
stops.note: Make this your introduction to the Kolob Canyons area, with exhibits on its geology, vegetation, and wildlife. The center is listed as closed daily from noon to 1 p.m.; ask rangers about places to explore before setting out farther.
stops.why: Kolob gives this day a different part of Zion rather than another morning in the main canyon.

stops.name: Human History Museum
stops.note: Back in the main canyon, linger outside for the views of the Towers of the Virgin and Bridge Mountain; this visit need not repeat the exhibits.
stops.why: It makes the return from Kolob a relaxed scenic afternoon rather than another scheduled indoor visit.

days.label: Zion–Mt. Carmel Highway and canyon history

stops.name: Zion-Mt. Carmel Highway
stops.note: Set aside an unhurried daytime drive on the highway between Canyon Junction and the East Entrance. Check road and tunnel status before you go; don't rely on a nighttime crossing.
stops.why: A day centered on the east-side road feels different from the visitor facilities and Kolob day.

stops.name: Human History Museum
stops.note: If you skipped the exhibits or film on day one, see them now; otherwise spend the time with the changing exhibits and the views outside.
stops.why: This is a flexible indoor-and-outdoor afternoon after time on the road.

days.label: Nature Center exhibits and a last canyon view

stops.name: Zion Nature Center
stops.note: If your dates fall during its summer season and it is open, explore the interactive exhibits on Zion’s habitats and wildlife; check its hours before making the trip over.
stops.why: The hands-on exhibits offer a quieter, different perspective on the park for your last day.

stops.name: Human History Museum
stops.note: Spend a final unhurried session outside framing the Towers of the Virgin and Bridge Mountain. If the Nature Center is unavailable, allow more time here for the museum’s exhibits too.
stops.why: You can revisit the canyon view without adding an unverified hike to the schedule.

claim.text: Human History Museum: Immerse yourself in the human history of Zion National Park! Rangers staff an information desk during operating hours. Indoor exhibits explore the people, places, and stories of Zion. Rotating exhibits feature regional artists, local discoveries, and more. A 22-minute orientation film examines the history of the canyon and highlights the dramatic landscapes of the park. Visit the bookstore for books, gifts, and souvenirs. There are also dramatic views of the Towers of the Virgin and Bridge Mountain outside.

Kolob Canyons Visitor Center: Closed daily from 12pm-1pm This is the entry point to the Kolob Canyons area of the park. It is located 45 miles north of Springdale and 17 miles south of Cedar City at Exit 40 on Interstate 15. Park rangers are available to answer questions. Exhibits explore the geology, vegetation, and wildlife of this unique landscape.

Zion Canyon Visitor Center: Located near the South Entrance of the park, the Zion Canyon Visitor Center is an excellent place to begin your exploration of Zion Canyon. Park rangers and outdoor exhibits will help you plan your visit and make the most of your time. Inquire at the Zion Canyon Wilderness Desk about permits for backpacking, canyoneering, and other trips into the wilderness. Visit the bookstore for maps, books, and gifts.

Zion Nature Center: During the summer, come visit the Zion Nature Center! This is a perfect place to learn about geology, animals, and the history of Zion. Take a break from the sun to explore different habitats, enjoy bird songs, listen to canyon tree frog calls, and participate in Junior Ranger programs. The inside of the Nature Center has a variety of interactive exhibits, animal models, changing activities, and crafts. Park rangers host educational programs throughout the day.

Large vehicle restrictions on Zion-Mt. Carmel Highway: Vehicles that exceed length, width, height, or weight limits cannot travel between Canyon Junction and the park's East Entrance. See the current limits on the page linked below.
